info.title: FlowPay API
info.description:
FlowPay is a digital wallet platform. This is the **public API**, reached through the gateway at
`http://localhost:8080`.

## Quick start
1. **Register** - `POST /api/v1/users`
2. **Log in** - `POST /api/v1/auth/login` -> copy the `accessToken`
3. Click **Authorize** (top right) and paste the token. Protected endpoints (padlock icon) now work.
4. **View / update your profile** - `GET` / `PATCH /api/v1/users/{id}`
5. **Verify your identity** - `GET /api/v1/kyc`, then `POST /api/v1/kyc/tiers/1` and `/tiers/2`. Your verification level decides what you may do with money.
6. **Open a wallet** - `POST /api/v1/wallets` (needs KYC level 1), then `GET /api/v1/wallets` to see your balances.
7. **Add money** - `POST /api/v1/funding`, then follow it with `GET /api/v1/funding/{reference}`. Your wallet is credited once the payment is confirmed.

## How security works
* Only registration, login, refresh, logout, password reset and the health check are public.
* Everything else needs `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Tokens are JWTs signed with RS256 and last 15 minutes;
  renew them with `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` (refresh tokens are single use).
* You only ever see and change **your own** data. Another customer's id returns `404`.
* Several endpoints are rate limited per IP address and return `429` with a `Retry-After` header when exceeded.
* Every error has the same shape: `{timestamp, status, error, message, path}`. Branch on `error`, not `message`.

## Emails in development
Password reset and two-step verification send real emails to a local inbox (Mailpit): http://localhost:8025.

tags.description: Register an account, then view and maintain your own profile.

tags.name: 2. Authentication
tags.description: Sign in, keep a session alive, and sign out.

tags.name: 3. Password reset
tags.description: Recover an account when the password is forgotten. Both steps are public.

tags.description: Optional extra security: after the password, a 6-digit code is emailed. All three calls need a bearer token.

tags.name: 5. Identity verification (KYC)
tags.description: Verify your identity to unlock more of FlowPay. Three levels: 0 (just registered), 1 (date of birth + address), 2 (government ID). All calls need a bearer token and only ever touch your own data.

tags.name: 6. Wallets
tags.description: Hold your money in a wallet. You need a verified identity (KYC level 1) to open one. All calls need a bearer token and only ever touch your own wallets.

tags.name: 7. Wallet funding
tags.description: Add money to your wallet. You ask to fund it, pay through the chosen source, and your wallet is credited once the payment is confirmed. All calls need a bearer token and only ever touch your own fundings.

post.summary: Log in with email and password
post.description:
Signs a customer in. **Public.** Limited to 10 attempts per minute per IP address (shared with `login/verify`).

### How it works
* Correct password, two-step verification **off** -> `200` with `accessToken` (JWT, 15 min) and `refreshToken` (7 days).
* Correct password, two-step verification **on** -> `200` with `{"mfaRequired": true, "challengeId": ...}` and **no tokens**. A 6-digit code is emailed; finish with `POST /api/v1/auth/login/verify`.
* Anything else -> the **same** `401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS` message for a wrong password, an unknown email and a locked account, so the API never reveals whether an account exists.
* **5 wrong passwords lock the account for 15 minutes** (even the correct password is refused while locked).

### How to test
1. Register a customer first (`POST /api/v1/users`).
2. Log in with the right password. Expect **200** and tokens. Copy `accessToken` into the Authorize box.
3. Log in with a wrong password. Expect **401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS**. Try an unknown email: the response is identical.
4. Fail 5 times in a row, then use the correct password. Still **401** (locked for 15 minutes; a password reset unlocks it).
5. Hit it 11 times in a minute. Expect **429**.
6. To try the two-step response, enable it under "4. Two-step verification" and log in again.

200.description: Tokens, or an MFA challenge when two-step verification is enabled.

401.description: INVALID_CREDENTIALS (wrong password, unknown email, or locked account).

503.description: MFA_UNAVAILABLE: two-step is on but the code email could not be sent. No tokens issued.

post.summary: Finish login with the emailed code
post.description:
Second step of login for customers who turned on two-step verification. **Public.** Shares the login rate limit.

### How it works
The code is 6 digits, valid **5 minutes**, usable **once**, with **5 guesses**. Wrong guesses also count towards the account lockout.
Every failure (wrong code, expired, already used, unknown challenge) returns the same `401 INVALID_MFA_CODE`.

### How to test
1. Enable two-step verification, then call `POST /api/v1/auth/login`. Copy `challengeId`.
2. Open the inbox (Mailpit at http://localhost:8025) and read the 6-digit code.
3. Send `challengeId` + `code`. Expect **200** with tokens.
4. Send the same code again. Expect **401 INVALID_MFA_CODE** (single use).
5. Request a new login code and send `000000` five times. The code is now dead, even the right one.
6. A malformed code such as `12ab` returns **400**.

Ends the session that the refresh token belongs to. **Public** (the refresh token is the proof).

### How it works
The refresh token (and every token in its chain) is revoked. Calling it again, or with an unknown token, still returns `204`, so it is safe to repeat and reveals nothing.
The access token already issued stays valid until it expires (at most 15 minutes).

### How to test
1. Log in and copy `refreshToken`.
2. Call logout with it. Expect **204**.
3. Call refresh with the same token. Expect **401**.
4. Call logout again. Still **204**.

204.description: Session ended (or there was nothing to end).

post.description:
Ends **every** session of the signed-in customer (phone, laptop, ...). **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
All of the customer's refresh tokens are revoked. Existing access tokens expire on their own within 15 minutes.

### How to test
1. Log in twice to create two sessions; keep both `refreshToken` values and one `accessToken`.
2. Call this endpoint with the access token. Expect **204**.
3. Call refresh with each refresh token. Both return **401**.
4. Call it without a token. Expect **401 UNAUTHENTICATED**.

Turns two-step verification off. **Requires a bearer token and the current password.**

### How it works
The password is required so that a stolen access token alone cannot weaken the account. Wrong passwords here count towards the account lockout.

### How to test
1. With two-step on, send a wrong password. Expect **401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS** (still enabled).
2. Send the correct password. Expect **204**.
3. Log in: you get tokens directly again.

post.summary: Confirm the code and turn on two-step verification
post.description:
Turns two-step verification on once the emailed code is proven. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
The code must belong to **your** account and to this purpose (a login code cannot be used here, and vice versa). Same rules as login codes: 5 minutes, single use, 5 guesses.
From then on, `POST /api/v1/auth/login` returns `mfaRequired` instead of tokens.

### How to test
1. After `enable/request`, send the `challengeId` and the emailed `code`. Expect **204**.
2. Log in again: the response is now `{"mfaRequired": true, ...}`.
3. Send a wrong code: **401 INVALID_MFA_CODE**.
4. Send a code that belongs to someone else's challenge: also **401**.

Emails a confirmation code. **Requires a bearer token.** Limited to 10 requests per minute per IP address (shared with the other MFA calls).

### How it works
A code is emailed first, so you cannot lock yourself out with an address that does not work. Nothing changes until you confirm the code.
Requesting again replaces the previous code. If two-step is already on you get `409`.

### How to test
1. Log in and authorize with the `accessToken`.
2. Call this endpoint. Expect **200** with a `challengeId`. Copy it.
3. Open the inbox (Mailpit at http://localhost:8025) and read the code.
4. Continue with `POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/enable/confirm`.
5. Without a token: **401**. After enabling, calling this again: **409 MFA_ALREADY_ENABLED**.

503.description: MFA_UNAVAILABLE: the code email could not be sent.

post.summary: Set a new password using the emailed token
post.description:
Completes a reset. **Public.** The emailed token is the proof of ownership.

### How it works
In one transaction: the token is used up (it works **once**), the password is changed, a locked account is **unlocked**, and **every session is signed out**. A "password changed" email is then sent.
Unknown, expired and already-used tokens all return the same `400 INVALID_RESET_TOKEN`.
A weak new password is rejected **without** using up the token, so you can retry.

### How to test
1. Request a reset and copy the `token` from the email.
2. Send `token` + a strong `newPassword`. Expect **204**.
3. Log in with the new password: **200**. With the old one: **401**.
4. Send the same token again: **400 INVALID_RESET_TOKEN**.
5. Try an old refresh token: **401** (everyone was signed out).
6. Send `newPassword: "weak"` with a fresh token: **400 VALIDATION_ERROR**, and the token still works afterwards.

post.summary: Email me a password reset link
post.description:
Asks for a reset link to be emailed. **Public.** Limited to 5 requests per minute per IP address (shared with `confirm`).

### How it works
* The answer is **always** `202` with the same message, whether or not the email has an account, so this cannot be used to find out who is registered.
* If the account exists, a one-time link valid for **30 minutes** is emailed (`PASSWORD_RESET_URL?token=...`). The email is sent in the background.
* Asking again cancels the earlier link; only the newest works.

### How to test
1. Register a customer, then call this endpoint with their email. Expect **202**.
2. Call it with an email that does not exist. Expect the **identical 202** body.
3. Open the inbox (Mailpit at http://localhost:8025). Only the real account received an email. Copy the `token=` value from the link.
4. Continue with `POST /api/v1/auth/password-reset/confirm`.

202.description: Accepted. The same response for every email.

post.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a fresh access token **and a new refresh token**. **Public** (the refresh token is the proof).

### How it works
Refresh tokens are **single use** ("rotation"). Using one returns a new pair and retires the old token.
If an already-used token is presented again it may have been stolen, so the **whole session is revoked**: every token in that chain stops working.

### How to test
1. Log in and copy `refreshToken`.
2. Call refresh with it. Expect **200** and a **different** `refreshToken`.
3. Call refresh again with the **old** token. Expect **401 INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN**.
4. Now try the **new** token from step 2. Also **401**: reuse ended the session. Log in again.

401.description: INVALID_REFRESH_TOKEN: unknown, expired, already used, or revoked.

get.description:
Your funding requests, newest first. **Requires a bearer token.** `limit` defaults to 20 (1 to 100).

### How to test
1. Start two fundings, then call this: both appear, newest first.
2. A new account gets an empty list. Without a token: **401**.

post.description:
Records a request to add money to one of your wallets and gives you a unique `reference`. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
* This call **does not add money**. It creates the funding as `PENDING`. Your wallet is credited only after the payment is confirmed.
* The wallet must be yours, in the same currency, and able to receive money (not `BLOCKED` or `CLOSED`).
* Your verification level must allow it: funding needs KYC level 1, and the amount must be within your level's limit. This is checked live every time.
* `source` is `BANK_TRANSFER`, `CARD` or `EXTERNAL_PROVIDER`.
* Follow the funding with `GET /api/v1/funding/{reference}`. Statuses: `PENDING`, `PROCESSING`, `SUCCESS` (money is in your wallet), `FAILED` (nothing was added), `REQUIRES_REVIEW` (our team is checking; your money is safe).

### How to test
1. Open a wallet and make sure you are verified to level 1.
2. Call this with your `walletId`, `{"amount":5000.00,"currency":"NGN","source":"BANK_TRANSFER"}`: **201**, status `PENDING`, with a `Location` header. Your wallet balance has **not** changed.
3. Complete the payment with the internal confirm endpoint (it plays the payment provider), then view the funding: `SUCCESS`, and the wallet shows the money.
4. Try someone else's wallet id: **404**. Wrong currency: **422** `CURRENCY_MISMATCH`.
5. Try an amount above your level's limit: **403** `KYC_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. While unverified: **403** `KYC_LEVEL_TOO_LOW`.
6. Amount `0`, negative or with more than 2 decimals: **400**. Without a token: **401**.

201.description: The funding was recorded as PENDING.

404.description: WALLET_NOT_FOUND (or it belongs to someone else).

503.description: WALLET_UNAVAILABLE or KYC_UNAVAILABLE: a check could not be made; nothing was recorded.

get.summary: See how a funding is going
get.description:
Shows one of your fundings. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
* `PENDING`: waiting for your payment to be confirmed. `PROCESSING`: payment received, crediting your wallet.
* `SUCCESS`: your wallet has the money. `FAILED`: nothing was added to your wallet (see `failureReason`).
* `REQUIRES_REVIEW`: something needs a person to check. Your money is not lost.
* Another customer's funding returns **404**, the same as one that does not exist.

### How to test
1. Start a funding and view it by its `reference`: **200**, `PENDING`.
2. An unknown reference or someone else's: **404** `FUNDING_NOT_FOUND`. Without a token: **401**.

Shows where each tier stands and what your current level allows. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
* `level` is the highest tier that is `VERIFIED` (0 if none). It is read live from the database on every call.
* Each tier is `NOT_STARTED`, `PENDING` (waiting for a reviewer), `REQUIRES_REVIEW` (an extra check is needed), `VERIFIED` or `REJECTED` (with the reviewer's reason).
* `capabilities` lists the operations your level allows and the largest single transaction.

### How to test
1. Log in and authorize with your `accessToken`.
2. Call this endpoint on a new account. Expect **200**, `level: 0`, both tiers `NOT_STARTED`, and no allowed operations.
3. Submit tier 1, then call it again: tier 1 is `PENDING`.
4. After a reviewer approves (see the internal review endpoints), `level` becomes 1 and the allowed operations appear.
5. Without a token: **401**.

post.summary: Submit tier 1: date of birth and address
post.description:
Starts tier 1 verification. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
* You must be **at least 18** (otherwise `422 KYC_NOT_ELIGIBLE`).
* The submission is saved as `PENDING` and waits for a human reviewer. Nothing is verified automatically.
* You can have **one** open tier 1 submission at a time (`409 KYC_ALREADY_SUBMITTED`), and cannot resubmit once verified (`409 KYC_ALREADY_VERIFIED`).
* If a reviewer **rejects** it you may submit again.
* When it is approved your level becomes 1 and your account moves from `PENDING_VERIFICATION` to `ACTIVE` (this happens a moment later, through an event).

### How to test
1. Send the example body. Expect **201** with status `PENDING`.
2. Send it again. Expect **409 KYC_ALREADY_SUBMITTED**.
3. Use a date of birth less than 18 years ago on a fresh account. Expect **422 KYC_NOT_ELIGIBLE**.
4. Send `{}` or a bad country such as `Nigeria`. Expect **400 VALIDATION_ERROR**.
5. Ask a reviewer to approve it (`POST /internal/kyc/submissions/{id}/decision`), then check `GET /api/v1/kyc` and your profile.

Starts tier 2 verification with a government-issued ID. **Requires a bearer token and a verified tier 1.**

### How it works
* Tier 1 must already be `VERIFIED`, otherwise `422 KYC_TIER_PREREQUISITE`.
* **NIN** and **BVN** must be exactly 11 digits. Spaces and dashes in the number are ignored.
* The ID number is **encrypted** before it is stored and is shown back to you **masked** (`*******8901`). No document images are collected.
* Saved as `PENDING` for a human reviewer. If the same ID has already been submitted by another customer it is silently marked `REQUIRES_REVIEW` for a closer look (you are not told why).
* One open submission at a time (`409`), and you cannot resubmit once verified (`409`).

### How to test
1. Before tier 1 is verified, send the example body. Expect **422 KYC_TIER_PREREQUISITE**.
2. After tier 1 is approved, send it again. Expect **201** with status `PENDING` and a masked number.
3. Send `{"idType":"NIN","idNumber":"123"}`. Expect **400** (too short). Send a 10-digit NIN: **400** (must be 11).
4. Send it again while pending: **409 KYC_ALREADY_SUBMITTED**.
5. After approval, `level` becomes 2.

Creates a FlowPay account. **Public** (no token needed). Limited to 5 requests per minute per IP address.

### How it works
1. The request is validated (see the field rules in the schema).
2. The email is lowercased. Email and phone number must each be unique.
3. The customer is saved with a generated `id` and status `PENDING_VERIFICATION`.
4. The password is sent to **auth-service**, which hashes it (BCrypt) and stores it. This service never stores or returns it.
5. If auth-service is unavailable the whole registration is rolled back and you get `503`: there is never an account without a way to log in.

### How to test
1. Send the example body. Expect **201**, and copy the `id` from the response.
2. Send the exact same body again. Expect **409 DUPLICATE_CUSTOMER** (same email, in any letter case).
3. Change only the email and keep the phone number. Still **409** (phone must be unique too).
4. Send `{}` or a weak password such as `weak`. Expect **400 VALIDATION_ERROR** listing each bad field.
5. Send 6+ requests within a minute from one machine. Expect **429** with a `Retry-After` header.
6. Next step: log in with `POST /api/v1/auth/login`.

201.description: Account created. The Location header points at the profile URL.

409.description: DUPLICATE_CUSTOMER: email or phone number already registered.

503.description: REGISTRATION_UNAVAILABLE: auth-service could not store the login. Nothing was created; retry.

get.description:
Returns the signed-in customer's own profile. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
The gateway verifies the access token and tells this service who is calling. You can only read **your own** profile:
any other id, and any id that does not exist, returns the same `404`, so the API never reveals which customers exist.

### How to test
1. Register (`POST /api/v1/users`) and log in (`POST /api/v1/auth/login`). Put the `accessToken` in the Authorize box (or the `Authorization: Bearer ...` header).
2. Call this endpoint with the `id` from registration. Expect **200** and your profile.
3. Call it with a different UUID, e.g. `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`. Expect **404 CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND**.
4. Call it with no token. Expect **401 UNAUTHENTICATED**.
5. Call it with `not-a-uuid`. Expect **400**.

400.description: MALFORMED_REQUEST: the id is not a valid UUID.

401.description: UNAUTHENTICATED: missing, expired or invalid access token.

404.description: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND: not your profile, or no such customer.

patch.description:
Changes the allowed parts of your profile. **Requires a bearer token.** Send only the fields you want to change.

### What you can change
| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `addressLine1`, `addressLine2`, `city`, `state`, `postalCode` | While the account is `PENDING_VERIFICATION` or `ACTIVE`. An empty string clears the field. |
| `firstName`, `lastName` | Only while `PENDING_VERIFICATION`. They lock once the account is verified. |
| `email`, `phoneNumber`, `country` | **Never** here (they need verification). Sending them returns `422 PROFILE_FIELD_LOCKED`. |
| Any field on a `SUSPENDED`, `BLOCKED` or `CLOSED` account | `422 ACCOUNT_NOT_EDITABLE`. |

### How to test
1. Sign in and use your `id`. Send `{"city": "Lagos", "addressLine1": "12 Marina Road"}`. Expect **200** with the new values.
2. Send `{"firstName": "Adaeze"}`. Expect **200** (a new account is still `PENDING_VERIFICATION`).
3. Send `{"email": "new@example.com"}`. Expect **422 PROFILE_FIELD_LOCKED**.
4. Send `{"city": ""}`. The city is cleared (`null`).
5. Send `{"firstName": "   "}`. Expect **400**.
6. Use another customer's id. Expect **404**. No token: **401**.
7. To see the name lock, set the account to ACTIVE in the database (there is no verification flow yet) and change `firstName` again: **422**.

404.description: CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND: not your profile, or no such customer.

409.description: CONCURRENT_UPDATE: another request changed the profile at the same moment; reload and retry.

get.description:
Every wallet you own, oldest first, including closed ones. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How to test
1. Open a wallet, then call this: it appears in the list.
2. A new account with no wallet gets an empty list.
3. Without a token: **401**.

post.description:
Opens an empty, `ACTIVE` wallet in one currency. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
* Only supported currencies are accepted (currently `NGN`). Anything else is refused.
* You must be verified to **level 1** or higher. This is checked live against the KYC service every time, never from the token.
* One live wallet per currency. A closed wallet does not stop you opening a new one.
* A new wallet has `ledgerBalance` and `availableBalance` of `0.00`. The available balance can never exceed the ledger balance and can never go below zero.

### How to test
1. Log in and authorize with your `accessToken`.
2. While still level 0, call this with `{"currency":"NGN"}`: **403** `KYC_LEVEL_TOO_LOW`.
3. Get verified to level 1 (see the KYC folder), then call again: **201** with a `Location` header and an `ACTIVE` wallet.
4. Call it again: **409** `WALLET_ALREADY_EXISTS`.
5. Try `{"currency":"USD"}`: **422** `UNSUPPORTED_CURRENCY`. Try `{"currency":"ngn"}` or `{}`: **400** `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
6. Without a token: **401**.

400.description: VALIDATION_ERROR: the currency is missing or malformed.

503.description: KYC_UNAVAILABLE: verification status could not be checked; nothing was created.

get.description:
Shows a wallet's balances and status. **Requires a bearer token.**

### How it works
* `ledgerBalance` is the recorded funds. `availableBalance` is what you can spend now; it is never more than the ledger balance.
* `status` is `ACTIVE`, `FROZEN`, `BLOCKED` or `CLOSED`. Only an `ACTIVE` wallet can send money. A `FROZEN` wallet can still receive money; `BLOCKED` and `CLOSED` wallets cannot.
* Another customer's wallet returns **404**, the same as one that does not exist.

### How to test
1. Open a wallet and call this with its `id`: **200**.
2. Call it with someone else's wallet id, or a random id: **404** `WALLET_NOT_FOUND`.
3. Without a token: **401**.

404.description: WALLET_NOT_FOUND (or it belongs to someone else).

maxSingleTransactionAmount.description: Largest single transaction this level may make.

CreateWalletRequest.description: Open a wallet in one currency.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Always explicit; never assumed. Only supported currencies are accepted.

CustomerProfileResponse.description: A customer's profile. Never includes any password data.

status.description: PENDING_VERIFICATION, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, BLOCKED or CLOSED.

CustomerResponse.description: The account that was just created.

id.description: Unique customer id. Use it in /api/v1/users/{id}.

DisableMfaRequest.description: Confirms the account owner before two-step verification is turned off.

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error body used by every endpoint.

error.description: Stable machine-readable code to branch on.

message.example: email must be a well-formed email address

FundingResponse.description: A request to add money to a wallet, and how it is going.

reference.description: Unique reference. Quote it when paying and when contacting support.

status.description: PENDING (waiting for the payment), PROCESSING (payment received, crediting your wallet), SUCCESS (your wallet has the money), FAILED (nothing was added), REQUIRES_REVIEW (our team is checking).

failureReason.description: Why it failed, when status is FAILED.

InitiateFundingRequest.description: Ask to add money to one of your wallets.

walletId.description: The wallet to fund. It must be yours.

amount.description: Amount, more than zero, at most 2 decimal places. Money is never a floating-point number.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency. Must equal the wallet's currency; never assumed.

KycStatusResponse.description: Your verification status, per tier, and what your current level allows.

level.description: Highest tier that is VERIFIED (0 if none).

message.example: If an account exists for that email, a reset link has been sent.

MfaChallengeResponse.description: A one-time code was emailed. Submit it with this challengeId to continue.

mfaRequired.description: Always true: the client must complete a second step.

challengeId.description: Identifies the emailed code. Send it with the code.

PasswordResetConfirmRequest.description: The token from the reset email plus the new password.

token.description: The value of ?token= in the emailed link. Single use, valid 30 minutes.

newPassword.description: 8-72 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a digit.

PasswordResetRequest.description: Asks for a password reset link to be emailed.

email.description: The account email. The response is identical whether or not it exists.

RefreshTokenRequest.description: A refresh token previously issued by login, login/verify or refresh.

refreshToken.description: The opaque refresh token. Each one works only once.

RegisterCustomerRequest.description: Details needed to open a FlowPay account.

email.description: Email address. Stored in lowercase and must be unique. Used to log in.

phoneNumber.description: Phone number in international format (E.164). Must be unique.

password.description: 8-72 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter and one digit. Hashed by auth-service; never stored or returned by user-service.

country.description: Country as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

status.description: Awaiting review shows as PENDING (or REQUIRES_REVIEW for extra checks).

rejectionReason.description: Why it was rejected. Only present when status is REJECTED.

maskedIdNumber.description: Tier 2 only: your ID number with all but the last 4 characters hidden.

SubmitTierOneRequest.description: Tier 1 verification: date of birth and residential address.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth (yyyy-MM-dd). You must be at least 18.

SubmitTierTwoRequest.description: Tier 2 verification: a government-issued ID. Requires tier 1 to be verified first.

idType.description: Kind of ID. NIN and BVN must be exactly 11 digits.

idNumber.description: The ID number. Spaces and dashes are ignored. Stored encrypted and shown masked.

TierStatusResponse.description: Where one tier stands. NOT_STARTED if you have not submitted it.

submissionId.description: Your latest submission for this tier, if any.

rejectionReason.description: Only present when status is REJECTED.

TokenResponse.description: A signed-in session: a short-lived access token and a single-use refresh token.

accessToken.description: JWT (RS256). Send as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Valid 15 minutes. The 'sub' claim is the customer id.

refreshToken.description: Opaque token valid 7 days. Exchange it at /refresh; each one works once.

UpdateCustomerProfileRequest.description: Fields to change. Omit a field to leave it unchanged; send an empty string to clear an optional address field. Email, phone number and country cannot be changed here.

firstName.description: Only changeable while the account status is PENDING_VERIFICATION.

lastName.description: Only changeable while the account status is PENDING_VERIFICATION.
